subject: Nonstandard GPU orchestration ask for LuminHealth pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@luminhealth.com>
Cc: ops@luminhealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Nonstandard GPU orchestration ask for LuminHealth pilot

Hi team,

Quick note to loop everyone on a short, nonstandard orchestration ask from LuminHealth's upcoming pilot (starts week of 11/23). They have a mixed workload: nightly batch synthesis jobs (large batch token volume, tolerant to 2–4 hour window) and daytime low-latency inference with bursty spikes for the telehealth UI (tight p95 latency).

Ask: they want a short-lived dedicated slice (1–2 A100-equivalent GPUs) with an autoscale policy exemption for 3 weeks so the nightly batches can run with sustained throughput without being preempted, while daytime calls get routed to the same slice for lower cold-start latency. We need product + infra alignment on:
- whether we can support a temporary autoscale waiver and what safeguards we require
- a fallback plan so daytime traffic fails over to hosted instances if the slice is saturated
- cost allocation + approval path (Lumin is open to a short-term reservation fee)

I attached the MOP/expected traffic matrix (lumin_pilot_mop.xlsx). Can we do a quick sync this week to finalize a runbook and sign-off?

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Program Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: lumin_pilot_mop.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@luminhealth.com>, ops@luminhealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nonstandard GPU orchestration ask for LuminHealth pilot

Thanks for the context, Soojin — this is doable but we need concrete numbers and a short checklist before product signs off. A few clarifying questions: 

1) Peak concurrent RPS and average tokens/sec during the nightly batch window? The MOP has ranges but we need a point estimate for config.
2) SLA expectations for daytime p95 latency and error budget (we need to know acceptable degradation when batch is running).
3) Exact start/end dates for the 3-week window and whether Lumin expects auto-renewal.
4) Do they require data plane isolation (VPC/private subnet), or is logical isolation sufficient?

If you can drop the numbers into the shared drive doc I linked (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_lumin-pilot-docs) I'll prepare a minimal product-runbook for approvals.

Quick thought: if infra can propose a safe autopause policy that preserves the nightly throughput but still surfaces saturation early, product can sign off faster.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@luminhealth.com>, ops@luminhealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nonstandard GPU orchestration ask for LuminHealth pilot

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 11:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> If you can drop the numbers into the shared drive doc I linked...

Thanks — did a quick run through constraints and options. TL;DR: infra can stand up a temporary sub-pool with a restricted scheduling class, and we can grant a temporary autoscale policy exemption for exactly the 3-week window with the following controls: 

- Restrict node reclamation: mark the nodes as "no-evict" for jobs tagged lumin_pilot_11_26 (prevents preemption by higher-priority training).
- CPU/tproc cap: night batches get a capped concurrency so we avoid a cascading outage if unexpected spike occurs.
- Daytime routing: setup a route rule — daytime calls routed by latency policy to the sub-pool; if p95 > 450ms for more than 3 consecutive minutes, failover to hosted pool (fail-open to preserve UX).
- Cost and telemetry: enforce token-level billing tags and add extra 30-day retention for traces for post-mortem.

I attached a sketch config: proposed-orchestration-config.yaml (stub). Implementation tasks: create Jira INFRA-4721, add quota exception, schedule a preflight load test (night mode) on 11/20.

Open questions for product: exact concurrency cap for nightly runs and whether Lumin wants guaranteed network isolation. If they want private VPC connect we need a new order and it bumps lead time by ~2 weeks.

-Mark
Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-orchestration-config.yaml (config, 3KB)
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@luminhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@luminhealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nonstandard GPU orchestration ask for LuminHealth pilot

Hi all — thanks for the quick turnaround. Apologies for the delay, pulled the point estimates from our infra team and uploaded the signed MOU to the drive. Highlights: 

- Nightly batch: target throughput 1.2M tokens/hour, typical sustained ~325 tokens/sec, peak blob windows up to 520 tokens/sec for 10–15 minutes.
- Daytime: expected peak bursts up to 75 concurrent users, average p95 target <= 350ms.
- Pilot window: 2026-11-23 through 2026-12-13 (3 weeks), no auto-renewal; we'll request extension if we need it.
- Isolation: logical isolation is acceptable for the pilot; we do not require VPC for this run.

We reviewed Marcus' config sketch and agree to the daytime failover rule. We'll also run the suggested preflight load test on 11/20 and share results. Attaching signed_mou.pdf. Please confirm the quota exception flow and whether a PO or short reservation invoice is needed — ops@luminhealth.com is cc'd.

Best,
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform, LuminHealth

Attachments: signed_mou.pdf (document, 48KB)
